notes:
Technical description of the accepted tree; it sets no deployment policy. Supply split, allocations, owners and chain come from the separately versioned launch policy.

TOKEN: LaunchToken (src/LaunchToken.sol), OpenZeppelin ERC20 v5.1.0, name 'Launch Guard', symbol GUARD, 18 decimals. Zero-argument constructor mints exactly 1,000,000,000 GUARD (10^27 minor units) once to msg.sender, the factory. No owner, mint, burn, pause, tax, proxy or selfdestruct.

HOOK: LaunchGuardHook (src/LaunchGuardHook.sol) extends the vendored v4-periphery BaseHook; solc 0.8.26, evm cancun, via_ir, optimizer 200 runs, bytecode_hash none. getHookPermissions returns exactly beforeInitialize and beforeSwap (address flags 0x2080 = 8320); the other twelve flags, including all four return deltas, are false, so liquidity changes and donations never reach the hook and it never returns a delta or overrides the LP fee. BaseHook restricts both callbacks to the PoolManager. No owner, setter, pause, upgrade, exemption or custody; the hook never holds funds or calls unlock, swap, take or settle.

CONSTRUCTOR (IPoolManager manager, IERC20 token): argument 0 is the launch chain's PoolManager, written as $poolManager. Argument 1 is the LaunchToken address: the constructor requires both addresses to have code, reads token.totalSupply() and stores the immutable maxBuyAmount = totalSupply / 100 = 10,000,000 GUARD, reverting InvalidConfiguration otherwise.

BLOCKING GAP, NOT RESOLVABLE IN THIS ASSIGNMENT: LaunchToken exists only after the factory deploys it inside the launch transaction, and a univ4_hook manifest can carry only $poolManager, a literal address or an integer in constructorArgs (a previous '$token' entry was refused for that reason). No literal address can be right in advance, so argument 1 is the zero address: the constructor then reverts InvalidConfiguration instead of binding the hook to a wrong token, and the deployer simulation fails safely until the deployer substitutes the fresh LaunchToken address or the hook is revised to learn the launch token from the pool key in beforeInitialize. The protected Hook floor, which constructs the attested creation code with no token at the baked-in address, cannot deploy this hook as built either. Only launch.json may change here; revising src/LaunchGuardHook.sol is the fix.

BEHAVIOUR: beforeInitialize reverts InvalidPool for a pool that does not name this hook or does not contain the launch token, AlreadyInitialized for a repeated PoolId, then records guardEndsAt[poolId] = block.timestamp + 86,400 s and emits GuardStarted. beforeSwap reverts PoolNotInitialized for an unknown PoolId. While block.timestamp < guardEndsAt it reverts BuyLimitExceeded(10,000,000 GUARD) for any swap whose output currency is the launch token and whose output would exceed 1% of total supply: an exact-output request above the cap, or an exact-input or oversized request whose previewed output exceeds the cap (src/libraries/SwapPreview.sol reproduces core SwapMath, tick traversal, LP and protocol fees and the trader's price limit from live PoolManager state). Exactly the cap is allowed. Sells, partial fills within the cap, liquidity changes and donations are never restricted; from guardEndsAt onward every swap passes. Per-swap limit only: several swaps, even in one transaction, can buy more in aggregate. The preview is read-only; its gas grows with crossed ticks.

POOL: currency0 native ETH, currency1 GUARD, static LP fee 3000 (0.3%), tickSpacing 60. initialPrice 79299443975792720780679863727831 is TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick(138180), about 1,001,800 GUARD per ETH (about 998 ETH fully diluted); the source fixes no price, so this tick-aligned value is chosen here and the factory seeds one-sided GUARD liquidity below it. The 24-hour guard starts at the factory's initialize call. The CREATE2 salt is mined per deployer and init code for flags 0x2080.

Local checks: forge build, forge test (72 tests incl. fuzz) and forge fmt --check pass offline.
